image_prompt.text: Brightly coloured barriers lining both edges of the track that physically stop a runner leaving it, as opposed to painted markings
Green grass verges and fall-away edges outside the barriers that penalise a runner who leaves the track
A grand finish line arch spanning the full width of the track at the end of the course
Ramps, long jumps across gaps and stepped platforms making up the tricky jump sections of the course
Rotating and swinging obstacles set along the track that runners have to dodge at speed
Rolling hills the long winding track climbs and drops over, with tunnels bored through the larger mounds for the track to run through

layout_placement.text: The round-ending detection zone under the finish arch, tripped the moment a runner crosses it
Recovery points along the course that restore a fallen runner to the track with position, orientation and zeroed velocity instead of restarting the run
Speed boost sections along the track that launch a runner faster through the stretch that follows

notes: Racing leads because the sentence is about a race track that ends at a finish line and is run for speed; Obby is named second because the jump sections and dodgeable obstacles are real and Racing has no rows for them. Obby's genre-wide P6 is not imported — Racing carries P6 on its own, so the route is unchanged either way.

Tunnels through the hills overhang the track, so terrain-relief routes P2 rather than P0 + tiered. P2 is not ready yet; if the tunnels can be open archways or cuttings instead, the whole build stays on P6. Deferred, not dropped.
powerup-buffs is layout-only, so the visible boost-strip decals on the track surface do not reach the image stream through it — the boost sections should be dressed as part of the track surface.
Vibrant cartoon art direction — green grass edges, colourful barriers, exciting track design — is a style request no layout option covers.

would have asked: Sounds like a timed obstacle race — one long point-to-point course from the start to a grand finish arch, winding over hills and through tunnels, with dodgeable obstacles, tricky jump sections, speed boost strips, colourful guardrails, grass verges that punish going off-track, and checkpoints so a fall doesn't restart the run. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: how the start works — a single start line or a multi-lane starting grid so several runners launch side by side. The prompt says nothing about it, so startpoint-line and spawn-grid were both left out rather than assumed.
would have asked: it's described as a minigame but no lobby is described — should there be a start hub where players gather between rounds, or does the course begin straight away?
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
